newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - Activity dwindles after jobs.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - Activity dwindles after jobs.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bond activity dwindled in late afternoon trading following an active session earlier, when the government released key U.S. economic data, players said.
Spreads to U.S. Treasuries remained unchanged across most maturities, players said.
"We spiked up for a bit after the numbers but then just kind of sat around," said one high-grade trader. "It's was a busy morning and a very quiet afternoon."
On Friday, the U.S. Labor Department reported that the U.S. unemployment rate fell to a 23-year low in May.
The U.S. Labor department reported a drop of 0.1 percent in the unemployment rate to 4.8 percent in May and an increase of 138,000 in payroll employment.
Economists had anticipated job growth of 219,000 and a 5.0 percent unemployment rate for May.

U.S. Treasury prices immediately see-sawed after the numbers, falling and then recovering as players debated whether the May labor market data pushed the Federal Reserve closer to another interest rate hike.
Treasuries ended higher with yields falling to three-month lows as buyers erased early losses incurred by the report.
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Tresury bond closed up 40/32 at 98-1/32 to yield 6.78 percent versus 6.88 percent on Thursday.
"Ever since the market rallied this morning its been very quiet ... seems like retail was sticker shocked," another high-grade trader said.
Meanwhile, on the new issue front, only one high-grade issuer tapped the public market despite more attractive financing rates, players said.
Anhueser-Busch Cos Inc sold $250 million in 10-year debt at 55 basis points over Treasuries via lead underwriter JP Morgan Securities.

In the private placement market, Peninsular & Oriental Steam Navigation Co issued $300 million in 10-year notes at 72 basis points and $200 million in 30-year debt at 100 basis points over Treasuries. The deal was underwritten by JP Morgan Securities, sources said.
Turning to the high-yield sector, prices closed about 1/2 point higher, players said.

"Junks ended on a high note but in the afternoon activity dwindled," said one trader. "I think what happened today was a lot of people left early...they didn't really get a chance to participate and watch the way stocks and governments moved."
"You should see the high-yield market do much better right out of the shoot on Monday," he said.
The Dow industrials surged 130 points to close at 7435 reaching a record high on Friday after the monthly employment report reinforced investors' positive outlook on the U.S. economy.
Among Friday's key gainers were Trump AC bonds, which traded up one point at par and Trump Castle debt, quoted up at a 90-3/4 bid, 91-3/4 offer, traders said.
Crowne paper also gained one point to trade at 102-1/8 bid, 102-5/8 offer, players said.
Falcon Building debt also traded up 1/2 point at 101-1/2 bid, 102 offer, trader said.
Also, Hechinger debt was quoted two points higher, they said.
In the supermarket sector, Pathmark Stores 11-5/8 percent paper traded up 1-1/2 at par and the 9-5/8 traded up at 95 bid. Brand Union paper was quoted at 81-1/2 bid, 82-1/2 offer, traders added.
